title: Butterfly on lavender in cross-stitch
subtitle: A peacock butterfly resting on a lavender stem, on 14-count Aida
excerpt: A butterfly on lavender is a 75-by-85 stitch piece on 14-count Aida. The peacock butterfly's vivid wing eye-spots and the soft purple lavender stem together use twelve floss colours. A small amount of back-stitch adds the antennae. Finished size is about 13 x 15 cm in a 15 cm hoop.
sourceNotes: Original design for Homemade cross-stitch library. Peacock butterfly wing markings are well documented in natural history illustration, including Humphrey's British Butterflies (1827), Internet Archive.

items.name: 14-count Aida, cream or white
items.substitutions: Very pale lavender Aida ties the background to the flower

content.text: Find the fabric centre. The chart centre falls approximately in the wing join (thorax). Begin there with the black wing border (310) to establish the four-wing outline.
Fill in the rust (900, 720) wing areas, then add the eye-spot details: the yellow centre (3823), blue ring (517), and outer black ring (310). Each eye-spot is roughly 5 x 5 stitches.
Work the three-quarter stitches at the forewing tip where the wing outline curves. Use 310 for the outer edge and 720 for the fill.
Stitch the lavender spike in the three purple-greens (209, 211 for the flower pip clusters, 3053, 522, 524 for the stem and sepals).
Add the antennae in a single strand of 3371 as two long back-stitch lines from the thorax upward. Club each antenna with two or three tiny back stitches in a small oval.
Wash gently in cool water and press face-down until the stitches sit smooth and flat. A white-painted frame or a natural wood mount with a purple linen mount suits the piece.

items.symptom: The wing colour graduation looks stripy rather than gradual
items.cause: Each colour was worked in a complete block before moving to the next shade.
items.fix: Work the graduation in diagonal rows that mix adjacent colours. Once both shades are blended in the transition row, the shift reads as smooth from a distance.

items.symptom: The lavender stems look like a solid mass
items.cause: The bud area was stitched with no variation between stem and flower colour.
items.fix: The bud tips should use the lighter purple; the calyx uses the grey-green. Work the tips first, then the calyx stitches around them. The piece is finished when the two-tone separation is visible in the bud cluster.

content.text: The florals sub-category has botanical companion pieces. A lavender stem on its own suits a small hoop. You can also pair this butterfly with a lavender spray in matching colours.

glossaryTerms.definition: A stiff, evenly-woven cross-stitch fabric with clearly visible squares formed by groups of threads. The default for beginners. Counted in squares per inch: 11ct, 14ct, 16ct, and 18ct are the common counts.

The six-strand embroidery thread used for cross-stitch. Each skein is made of six strands twisted together loosely; the stitcher strips out the number of strands needed for the fabric count (two strands for 14-count Aida) and threads them together.

A solid outline stitch worked in a single strand along the back-stitch layer of the chart. You stitch backwards along the line one stitch at a time, each stitch finishing where the previous one started.
